questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My exchange plans were cancelled twice due to covid. I therefor had to apply for remaining places of which Sorbonne in Paris was the best option. Furthermore due to my language skills and previous experience in France I knew that I wanted to improve my French and experience studying in France.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The process of applying for and going on exchange was horrible. The collaboration between KU, the host university and Erasmus was very bad especially due to lack of communication and the intersections between the three administrations - which can definitely be improved as all the problems effect the students. However while I was in France the experience was great and I would recommend everyone to go on exchange.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very difficult and cryptic information available to the students who are going on exchange in Europe. When I was going to Sydney more information was available to the students. I found the process very stressful and irritating due to the lack of information with regards to courses available, dates, documents needed etc. I would recommend that the travel reports from the previous erasmus students are published for the new students applying for exchange.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Almost no assistance. We got information very late in the process, and I had a lot of questions which were difficult to get answers to without forcing the administration to respond by mail or by phone. We only limited information about the introduction week and it was impossible to figure out which courses were available to erasmus students. Furthermore, there were no counselling for Erasmus students nor any mentors in charge of showing us around etc. However the Erasmus organisation hosted really nice events for the students in generel, and I loved living in Paris, meeting new people and studying in another country, which is why I would still recommend going despite all the problems with the process and administration.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The French system in general is very bad with horrible digitalisation and lack of information. This was also reflected at the host university. However I still had a great experience in France.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived in the Cité Universitaire which was a great experience and also very easy to apply for.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living in Cité Universitaire was nice with lots of events and students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was really bad since no one responded to my emails, and when they did they told me to contact someone else. I found the process very stressful and irritating due to the lack of information with regards to courses available, dates, calendar, documents needed etc. Almost no assistance. We got information very late in the process, and I had a lot of questions which were difficult to get answers to without forcing the administration to respond by mail or by phone. We only limited information about the introduction week and it was impossible to figure out which courses were available to erasmus students.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email, however it was really difficult.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had to change courses a few time, and there werent a lot of courses available for erasmus students, which is a shame.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have patience and try to remember that France is a fucked up and lovely country at the same time ;) The registration process is horrible, but it is worth it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The French courses are at a higher level than the English courses - having taken both, I found that the English courses where there in order for the French students to learn English rather than to learn the actual content of the course. Please note that the French courses are solely in French, also the exams, however they are much more advanced and interesting than the English courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Since we were only allowed to take courses with lectures and no small classes, the teaching was very different to the courses on UCPH. Furthermore, the university doesnt have much control with the professors, which means that some professors are really motivated, engaged and keen to create the best course (eg. politique etrangere and  introduction to post-socialist europe), while some professors seem like they dont really want to be there and dont really care if we learn anything. However, as a result I think some of my courses were brilliant and some were absolutely horrible.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Comparative European Politics, International Finance, Politique Etrangere, Politique, Religion et Radicalization, Introduction to Post-socialist Europe, Critical Approaches.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Politique Etrangere, Politique, Religion et Radicalization, Introduction to Post-socialist Europe

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: sports - however most social activities were hosted by Erasmus which were great!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Going on excursions to see more of France.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: travel around France, and go to all the great museums in Paris.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - however you realise how bad the french system is compared to the danish.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They didnt really seem to be interested in getting to know exchange students - therefor I made a lot of friends from other countries that I had classes with and that I met in the first week. Furthermore I met a lot of Danish people at Cité Universitaire.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: the lazyness and the administrative burdens haha

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the life in Paris, all the nice places, the vibe, the experience, the vibrant culture, the way of living! Couldnt recommend it enough!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Have patience, enjoy it and live life to the fullest - the academics are not worth stressing about!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The exams are VERY different from the Danish exams at political science. They are all "closed book" sit-in exams written by hand (a pen) and some of them are oral exams, in which you have no guidance. I had 6 exams in 8 days and they are very short and weirdly structured.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting different people, making friends for life, and experiencing the real, local Paris with all its ups and downs. I definetely want to come back to Paris!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The system and the administration. An example: in order to cancel my phone operator called "Free" I had to call a phone number, where they gave me a physical postal address to which I had to send a physical letter stating that I wanted to cancel my subscription. An other example: In order to apply for the courses I wanted I had go to the same office three times, send 10 emails, and call three different people before the deadline.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Please go on exchange, you will regret it if you dont! It is a once in a life time experience.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
